title: Coalesce credential lifecycles, retry DSL, and stream checkpoints across Py/TS/Go SDKs
author: Maya Tran
description: This PR harmonizes three adjacent SDK concerns across Python, TypeScript, and Go: credential lifecycle primitives, a small opinionated RetryProfile DSL, and an explicit StreamCheckpoint primitive for resumable streaming consumers. Motivation: customer signals and internal telemetry showed recurring integration pain when apps attempted to (a) compose credential refresh strategies with streaming consumers, (b) surface retry intent consistently across languages, and (c) resume long-lived streams after transient auth failures. This changeset introduces: 1) credential.Conductor / credential.ConductorOptions (py/ts/go) — a small surface that centralizes TTL/lease semantics, prefetch hooks, and preferred fallback chains; 2) RetryProfile: a declarative retry preseter (fast-fail / conservative / latency-sensitive) and a lightweight compiler that maps profiles to transport-level backoffs and jitter seeds; 3) StreamCheckpoint: a compact resume token + consumer hint structure that SDKs attach to streaming responses so applications can checkpoint/resume with semantics aligned across languages. Implementation notes: - The runtime bindings were kept intentionally small; heavy lifting remains in the platform. - Default RetryProfile maps to previous SDK defaults to avoid changing existing behavior for current users. - Added explicit opt-in for StreamCheckpoint persistence; no background persistence is performed by SDKs. - Version bumps: Python -> 1.33.0, TypeScript -> 2.18.0, Go -> v1.9.0. Upgrade guidance is included in release_notes. The description below lists commits, changed files, reviewers discussion excerpts, and CI outcomes.
commits: feat(cred): add Conductor primitive and options with prefetch/fallback hooks
feat(retry): introduce RetryProfile DSL and profile-to-backoff compiler
feat(stream): attach StreamCheckpoint to streaming envelopes and add resume helpers
fix(ts): align auth TTL typing across TS SDK and docs examples
chore(py): bump py SDK to 1.33.0, update changelog
chore(ts): bump ts SDK to 2.18.0, regenerate types
chore(go): bump go SDK to v1.9.0, export Connector interfaces for resume helpers
test: add cross-sdk contract tests for RetryProfile semantics
docs: add migration notes and examples for credential conductor and stream checkpoints
review_comments: Carlos Estevez: Overall shape looks good. Please add an explicit note in the TS types about the nullable resumeToken so downstream consumers don't accidentally persist empty checkpoints.
Maya Tran (author): Good catch, added nullable guard comments and a short unit test covering empty-token behavior.
Rina Patel: Can we make RetryProfile extensible without breaking default binary mapping? Suggest adding a "custom" bucket that requires explicit compilation step.
Maya Tran (author): Added a "Custom" enum member and a compile_with hook; documented in the migration guide. Kept default unchanged.
Liam O'Connor: Go SDK exported connector interface is necessary, but please ensure consumers can still use the previous Connector concrete type for simple cases.
Maya Tran (author): Preserved old connector constructor and added a thin adapter to satisfy the new interface; added a deprecation note and tests.
release_notes:
- Introduced credential.Conductor (py/ts/go) to simplify TTL and prefetch lifecycles.
- Added RetryProfile DSL with three built-in profiles (fast-fail, conservative, latency-sensitive) and a Custom extension point.
- StreamCheckpoint primitive enables safe resume semantics for streaming consumers; opt-in persistence.
- SDK version bumps: Python 1.33.0, TypeScript 2.18.0, Go v1.9.0.
Migration notes: see sdks/shared/docs/migration/cred-retry-stream.md for step-by-step upgrade guidance. Backwards compatibility: defaults map to previous runtime behavior; read the migration doc before adopting Custom RetryProfile or enabling automatic resume persistence.
notes: This change was driven by customer integrations with long-running streaming ingestion pipelines and by internal telemetry highlighting inconsistent retry behavior across the language SDKs. The crosslang contract tests exercise the profile mappings to avoid drift in future changes.
